heading: Representations become more aligned as models grow larger and more capable
definition: as models get larger and more capable, the representations of independently trained models with different architectures, objectives and data become more aligned.
summary: The broad claim that alignment increases with model scale is contested: independent studies find increases in some settings, but trends depend on model family, data and measurement. Trends can weaken or disappear after calibration, which corrects for baseline effects in the measurement.

suggested_status.by_scale: C for the unrestricted claim at <1B, 1-10B and 10-100B, with positive results conditional on setting and measure. Toy/synthetic evidence is conditional; counts have no separate toy size bucket. >100B: ? because no identified coverage is recorded.
suggested_status.reason: Calibrated global trends weaken or disappear in arXiv:2602.14486#r1/#r3/#r23; recent-model and dense-gallery extensions fail in arXiv:2604.18572#R8/#R12/#R13; language-size gains are non-monotonic or small and COCO scaling is challenged in arXiv:2610.39302; EEG scaling depends on metric and temporal-null calibration in arXiv:2611.05097#R4/#R11/#R12. Positive local and functional results remain in the synthesis. counts: versions.V1.verdicts.supports.studies=54, versions.V1.verdicts.limits_scope.studies=43 and versions.V1.verdicts.challenges.studies=17 are overlapping categories, not votes. versions.V1.studies_by_size and versions.V1.coverage_by_operation.scaling.by_size identify <1B, 1-10B and 10-100B coverage but no >100B entry. The contested level concerns the broad unqualified statement.
suggested_status.open_questions: A controlled architecture/objective/data scale experiment with independent capability measurements, prespecified preprocessing and layer aggregation, density-aware neighborhoods, calibrated local and global measures, and evaluation across recent model populations would clarify which scaling relationship generalizes. Joint-partner domain sweeps, stage-controlled reasoning/preference sweeps and identified >100B tests remain open.

source.title: The Platonic Representation Hypothesis
source.authors: Minyoung Huh; Brian Cheung; Tongzhou Wang; Phillip Isola

original_result.setup: In the original study, Huh et al. measured how often models share nearest neighbors (mutual-nearest-neighbor alignment) on Places-365 images and WIT image–caption pairs.
original_result.result: Among 78 vision models, groups with higher performance on the VTAB vision benchmark had greater average alignment. Image–caption alignment increased with language-model evaluation scores and tended to increase with vision-model performance.
original_result.interpretation: This is the displayed original-result block, not a guarantee that the original tested every part of this claim.

untested.what: A controlled factorial scale test independently varying architecture, objective and training data while measuring capability and alignment.
untested.basis: Untested-parts lines restrict arXiv:2607.14144 to shared corpus/tokenizer, arXiv:2304.13098 to matched topology/objective/data, and arXiv:2411.05316 to confounded size/family/dimension. arXiv:2606.16897 leaves data overlap unresolved. counts: versions.V1.studies_by_family and versions.V1.coverage_by_operation.scaling.by_family establish family coverage, not independently crossed factors.

untested.what: Identified scaling coverage above 100B parameters and extrapolation toward a universal limiting representation.
untested.basis: counts: versions.V1.studies_by_size and versions.V1.coverage_by_operation.scaling.by_size have no >100B entry. Untested-parts lines in arXiv:2609.24209 and arXiv:2605.28870 leave frontier extrapolation open. Unspecified-size entries prevent treating the missing bucket as verified absence for every record.

untested.what: Dedicated scale sweeps through reasoning or preference/RL stages, disentangled from base-model scale.
untested.basis: counts: versions.V1.coverage_by_operation.scaling.by_stage has no reasoning or preference/RL entry. versions.V1.studies_by_stage includes reasoning, so the gap concerns scaling rather than all representation measurements. The checker confirms that arXiv:2604.18572 Supplement F.3 separately evaluates recent base and post-trained populations with the original regression fixed; both subsets have negative predictive R² on every benchmark. These population splits do not provide controlled scale sweeps through training stages.

untested.what: The Qwen3 sensory-cue scale trend under no-cue generative or single-pass representations.
untested.basis: arXiv:2510.02425 untested-parts and not-in-rows lines restrict the stated scale result to matched cues and 128-token generative representations. Other trajectories lack a recorded scaling conclusion. counts: versions.V1.coverage_by_operation.scaling.by_family does not identify cue-specific coverage.

untested.what: Whether independently measured capability predicts alignment of mature decoder emotion geometry.
untested.basis: The checker reports no independently measured capability–alignment analysis in arXiv:2604.11050: §2.7 screens behavioral constraint-following scenarios, while §3.5 relates size and width to geometric descriptors. This is an unreported analysis, rather than an explicit open question stated by the study. Its mature-model size comparison reports no upward alignment shift and therefore belongs in against. arXiv:2606.00129#R1, arXiv:2606.00129#R2, arXiv:2606.00129#R3 and arXiv:2606.00129#R4 report inter-LLM valence-direction agreement without testing its trend with size or capability; Appendix S3's nonsignificant scaling correlation concerns human behavioral valence. counts: versions.V1.tested_with_capability_check does not establish this specific capability–alignment test.

untested.what: Protein text–structure and EEG cross-modal convergence as both partners independently improve in capability.
untested.basis: The checker distinguishes arXiv:2411.05316 RQ1's LLM-size comparisons against fixed geometric models from RQ4 and Figure 2C, which vary retrained GearNet embedding dimensions against the evaluated LLMs. Independent capability improvement of both partners is not established. untested.what: Whether the EEG foundation-model capability association generalizes beyond NICE marker decodability.
untested.basis: arXiv:2611.05097 untested-parts explicitly identifies broader capability as untested; its positive capability rows are R1, R2 and R8. The separate emotion-classifier valence study uses different models and a restricted representation object. counts: versions.V1.tested_with_capability_check does not distinguish capability definitions.

untested.what: Scale-dependent alignment between independently trained models in the astronomy cross-survey setting.
untested.basis: arXiv:2610.04130#r6, arXiv:2610.04130#r7, arXiv:2610.04130#r8, arXiv:2610.04130#r10 and arXiv:2610.04130#r11 regress cross-survey alignment within each pretrained model, controlling width, survey and family. wording_issues.phrase: as models get larger and more capable
wording_issues.issue: Parameter size, capability, task diversity and training progress are distinct axes. ConvNet width accompanies lower PWCCA distance and higher accuracy. ANN–SNN comparisons show increasing alignment with width but divergence with depth, including improved accuracy for deeper ResNets. Task-count changes at fixed transformer size and fixed-size ResNet-50 training trajectories do not test V1's model-scale trend.

Direct architecture scaling shares corpus/tokenizer; ANN–SNN scaling matches topology/objective/data; within-family EEG scaling shares architecture, data and objectives. Broad vision comparisons retain family clusters. These tests do not independently establish convergence across all stated differences.

The direction depends on metric, preprocessing and calibration. Unbiased CKA loses its association after calibration on the full vision–language model grid. Strict distance agreement weakens the vision-axis association and gives a descriptively negative correlation, without establishing a general inverse scaling relationship. A preprocessing condition reverses the CKA trend. Within-family EEG scaling increases under mKNN, whereas CKA increases only for FEMBA, with no increase for LUNA, NeuroLM or ST-EEGFormer. Temporal-control calibration removes the cross-modal EEG size trend.

Reported similarity can concern selected task subspaces, one valence direction, emotion RDMs or output-neighbor geometry. These restricted objects do not establish increasing similarity of complete input representations. Pooled Qwen3 valence agreement, individual emotion-model pairs and the single output-neighbor comparison do not establish a trend with scale or capability.

Learned-map retrieval, projected cosine separation and functional transfer measure different outcomes after fitting interfaces. Protein text–structure cosine separation after learned projections shows a V1 scale trend in the cited GearNet comparisons, with matched untrained baselines, but does not establish low-loss interchangeability. Alpaca generation through a fitted interface measures source-capacity dependence under V4 and leaves V1 undetermined. These outcomes do not directly establish intrinsic geometric convergence.

Growing absolute neuron-match counts coexist with shrinking shared fractions in the tested language-model comparisons. The phrase leaves unspecified whether alignment means an absolute count or a fraction of neurons; these measurements do not establish increasingly complete alignment of whole representations.

An unqualified positive direction does not fit DINOv3 reversals, object-universality null associations, absent vision-size trends or absent positive base-to-large SAE scaling. The SAE study describes base and large scores as very similar, with base slightly higher; this does not establish a reliable reversal. CKA null trends challenge the predicted increase, while borderline DESI CKA and partial full-basket MKNN results qualify its scope.

High existing similarity does not demonstrate continued increase. Individual emotion-model pairs and pooled mature-model similarity do not establish a scale trend; the separate mature-decoder comparison reports no upward shift when larger models are included. Pooled Qwen3 valence agreement is near ceiling but does not measure its trend with size. Later world-model alignment can plateau or decrease on PushT, Wall, Rope and Granular; PointMaze is absent from that later-checkpoint figure.

method_sensitivity.factor: Metric family, permutation calibration and regularization
method_sensitivity.what: Linear CKA capability correlation changes 0.86→0.45 and unbiased CKA 0.65→−0.01 after calibration, versus mKNN 0.85→0.84. Unbiased CKA uses the full grid of 204 vision–language pairs. Astronomy and COMPASS also show weaker global than local trends; COMPASS varies partner parameter count with fixed references. Under GULP λ=10−6, large-width, small-depth MNIST networks are the most different, reversing the width-convergence prediction; this qualification is verdict-only.

BLOOMZ mid-depth mKNN size trend is 0.84 under PRH preprocessing and −0.92 under plain ℓ2. CKA after permutation-mean subtraction is 0.70 (one-sided p=0.117; non-significant), versus −1.00 under plain ℓ2. Layer-max CKA under scal changes raw trends 0.89→−0.02 for BLOOMZ, 0.68→−0.85 for LLaMA-1, 0.88→0.18 for OpenLLaMA and 0.93→0.89 for Pythia. OpenLLaMA permutation-mean subtraction instead gives −0.59. Calibration therefore removes, reverses, weakens or preserves the size trend depending on family and procedure; Pythia does not show the predicted calibration-induced loss. Layer maxima also favor deeper models in the Pythia/Mamba/RWKV analysis.

Tighter distance agreement reduces scaling associations, including the descriptive vision-global change from 0.850 at τ=1 to −0.174 at τ=10−4. The tests establish weakening rather than a general inverse scaling relationship. Fixed k=10 loses the capability trend in WIT-1M. Increasing neuron-matching k raises match counts while preserving sublinear count growth: Pythia–OPT exponents are 0.68 at k=1 and 0.75 at k=2; diffusion–OpenCLIP exponents are 0.63 and 0.61 respectively. Thus counts depend on k without the scaling trend disappearing.

method_sensitivity.factor: Input information, uniqueness and view quality
method_sensitivity.what: Capacity–alignment associations weaken with modality-specific information and disappear in the synthetic U=8 condition. For MAE at U=90, the association remains weakly positive: slope=0.008 and average Spearman ρ=0.134, without a reported null test. Good-view JEPA data-scaling gains contrast with flat bad-view scaling: at q=0, WIT alignment remains 0.054–0.057 across 0.41M–50.9M images. This is an exposure-data comparison rather than a model-size sweep.

Recent-model extrapolation partially works on HellaSwag/Wikitext under mutual kNN while failing on reasoning/knowledge benchmarks. Phi-3 inclusion changes the visual-generalization/MMLU-Pro correlation from Pearson r=0.768 excluding Phi-3 to 0.523 including it. THINGS alignment depends on demonstrations. Qwen3's reported vision scale trend compares sizes under the same SEE cue, fixed DINOv2 and 128-token generation; smaller Qwen3 sizes provide the scaling baseline, with 0.6B the smallest tested. No cue is a separate condition.

method_sensitivity.factor: Feature selection, extraction and population normalization
method_sensitivity.what: SAE matching gives lower validation rates for small-model tiers, whereas optimized raw CCA/Procrustes cosines overlap across tiers. Base-to-large wMPPC depends on layer aggregation and mapping direction. Absolute neuron counts and shared fractions move in opposite directions with scale.

ANN–SNN width scaling increases CKA while depth scaling decreases it, with final-layer qualifications in very wide models and irregular layer-dependent results. RNN width convergence holds under µP with feature learning controlled, while the widest standard-parameterized 3BFF model reverses the dynamical trend. The latter is an opposite width-scaling outcome; the static SVCCA account does not establish a size-specific direction.

method_sensitivity.factor: EEG metric, partner modality and temporal-null calibration
method_sensitivity.what: Within-family EEG size increases raise calibrated mKNN but raise CKA only for FEMBA. NICE decodability associates with language alignment under CKA but not consistently under mKNN; vision associations are inconsistent overall. Circular-shift calibration removes the demonstrated FEMBA–DINOv2 raw-mKNN size trend; aggregate calibrated cross-modal comparisons lack a size association.

method_sensitivity.factor: Protein partner and world-model reference choices
method_sensitivity.what: Protein scale gains after learned heads occur for GearNet/GVP/ScanNet but not GAT. These results measure cosine separation after learned projections, with matched untrained baselines, rather than low-loss interchangeability. World-model scores and some rankings change with anchor, environment, checkpoint and encoder versus predictor space. ResNet remains near a low baseline without clear convergence. Later-checkpoint results cover PushT, Wall, Rope and Granular, around epochs 20, 30 and 50, with epoch 49 used for two PushT runs; they do not include a PointMaze panel. World-model comparisons concern training progress rather than a model-size sweep.
